parsed_explanation: The God Class anti-pattern is evident in the BRawInfo class, which exhibits excessive responsibilities and a large number of methods and properties. This class handles a wide range of functionalities, including managing raw percentages, validating raw structures, calculating contributions, and more. The impact of this anti-pattern includes poor maintainability, reduced readability, and increased risk of bugs due to the class's complexity and size.

This class is a God Class because it concentrates too many responsibilities in one place: domain state, serialization/deserialization, string/code mapping, cloning/factory logic, calculation helpers, validation/mutability rules, and even dependency resolution. It also exposes many virtual members that subclasses override in different ways, which makes the base class hard to understand, hard to test, and fragile to change. Any modification to one concern risks breaking unrelated behavior, and the large switch statements and many optional overrides indicate the type is acting as a central hub rather than a focused abstraction.

The God Class anti-pattern occurs when a single class has too many responsibilities, making it difficult to maintain and extend. In this case, the `BBegrotingTabel` class implements multiple interfaces (`IBegrotingTabel`, `IFCTabel`, `IRegelTabel`, `IBijzondereTabel`, `IInitialiseerHierarchie`, `IVerborgenKolommenTabel`) and has a large number of methods, making it a God Class. This can lead to tight coupling, low cohesion, and increased complexity.
parsed_suggested_fix: To refactor this class, identify the distinct responsibilities and extract them into separate classes, each with its own interface. For example, create a `BegrotingTabel` class that implements `IBegrotingTabel`, a `FCTabel` class that implements `IFCTabel`, and so on. This will help to reduce the complexity of the original class and improve maintainability. Additionally, consider using composition instead of inheritance to reduce coupling between classes. For instance, instead of having `BBegrotingTabel` implement `IFCTabel`, create a `FCTabel` class that is composed of a `BBegrotingTabel` instance.
